sessions.learningSummary: 本轮更偏好开头直接点名目标星座，并用短、直白的句子连接到广泛可认领的行为或关系张力。过长、抽象的反差表达较弱；“care deeply”这类心理判断应压缩并落到明显行为上。

candidates.title: Taurus Doesn't Rush Big Decisions
candidates.topic: Taurus decision-making and resistance to pressure
candidates.angle: Reverse the “Taurus is stubborn” stereotype by framing their refusal to rush as a deliberate standard.
candidates.copy: Taurus isn't slow—they just refuse to make big decisions under pressure.
candidates.testedVariable: Reverse-stereotype framing

candidates.title: The Taurus Silence Signal
candidates.topic: Taurus silence and changing their mind
candidates.angle: Use a recognizable communication behavior to show how Taurus may signal discomfort without openly arguing.
candidates.copy: When Taurus gets unusually quiet, they may already be rethinking the whole situation.
candidates.testedVariable: Behavior-to-consequence framing

candidates.title: Taurus Has a Line You Won't See Coming
candidates.topic: Taurus boundaries and non-negotiable priorities
candidates.angle: Create tension by contrasting Taurus’s calm exterior with the firmness of their private limits.
candidates.copy: Taurus can look easygoing right up until you ask them to give up the one thing they decided was non-negotiable.
candidates.testedVariable: Contrast and escalation

candidates.title: How Taurus Shows They Care
candidates.topic: Taurus loyalty and consistent effort
candidates.angle: Challenge the idea that Taurus only values comfort by connecting their loyalty to consistent effort rather than romantic clichés.
candidates.copy: Taurus doesn't always say they care—they keep showing up after everyone else gets tired.
candidates.testedVariable: Action-based emotional proof

nextCandidates.title: Taurus Remembers More Than You Think
nextCandidates.topic: Taurus showing care through memory and consistent attention
nextCandidates.angle: Show Taurus care through a simple, repeatable action rather than words.
nextCandidates.copy: Taurus shows they care by remembering the little things you thought they forgot.

nextCandidates.title: When Taurus Stops Arguing
nextCandidates.topic: Taurus withdrawing effort after repeated relationship conflict
nextCandidates.angle: Frame Taurus’s refusal to engage as a sign that the relationship may already be over for them.
nextCandidates.copy: When Taurus stops arguing, they may have already stopped trying.

nextCandidates.title: Why Taurus Takes So Long to Answer
nextCandidates.topic: Taurus delaying responses while reassessing trust
nextCandidates.angle: Use a direct question to make viewers recognize Taurus’s private decision process.
nextCandidates.copy: Why does Taurus take so long to answer? They may be deciding whether they still trust you.

nextCandidates.title: What Taurus Is Really Stubborn About
nextCandidates.angle: Use a compact reverse-stereotype claim that turns stubbornness into follow-through.
nextCandidates.copy: Taurus isn't stubborn about everything—they're committed to what still matters to them.

candidates.title: When Plans Change
candidates.topic: Why Taurus can go quiet when plans suddenly change, even if they eventually agree to the new plan
candidates.angle: Test whether a specific response to sudden change creates stronger recognition than generic “stubborn Taurus” framing.
candidates.copy: Taurus may not resist every change—they may need time to feel steady before they respond. This explores what happens when plans shift before they are ready.
candidates.testedVariable: Change-response framing versus a broad stubbornness label

candidates.title: Taurus Meets Gemini
candidates.topic: Why Taurus and Gemini can misunderstand each other when one wants a settled plan and the other wants to stay spontaneous
candidates.angle: Use a two-sign relationship mismatch to show how Taurus’s need for predictability can be misread as lack of interest by Gemini.
candidates.copy: Taurus may want time to settle into a plan, while Gemini wants to keep options open. The tension is not always about caring less—it can be about moving at different speeds.
candidates.testedVariable: Two-sign misinterpretation versus single-sign psychology

candidates.title: Taurus Moon Care
candidates.topic: How Taurus Moon shows love through comfort and practical care instead of dramatic emotional gestures
candidates.angle: Test a placement-led topic that translates Taurus Moon needs into observable relationship behavior rather than abstract emotional language.
candidates.copy: A Taurus Moon may show care through comfort, consistency, and practical support. This angle looks at why grand emotional declarations may matter less than feeling genuinely at ease.
candidates.testedVariable: Moon placement specificity versus Sun-sign relatability

candidates.title: The Taurus Exit Point
candidates.topic: Why Taurus can take a long time to leave a relationship or situation once it no longer feels right
candidates.angle: Frame delayed decisions as a boundary and self-protection question, avoiding labels like passive or indecisive.
candidates.copy: Taurus may stay in a situation longer than others expect because leaving means giving up something familiar and tangible. This explores the moment patience becomes a choice to protect stability.
candidates.testedVariable: Decision-threshold framing versus indecisiveness framing

nextCandidates.title: Taurus Needs Proof
nextCandidates.topic: Why Taurus may stay emotionally reserved until someone proves they are consistent over time
nextCandidates.angle: Frame Taurus hesitation as a trust response: they may need repeated proof before becoming fully open, rather than simply being guarded.
nextCandidates.copy: Taurus may seem hard to get close to, but the real issue can be consistency. This explores why steady actions often matter more to them than intense promises.

nextCandidates.title: Taurus in Conflict
nextCandidates.topic: Why Taurus may go quiet during an argument and return only after they have processed what they feel
nextCandidates.angle: Show how Taurus handles conflict through delayed, controlled responses instead of immediate emotional confrontation.
nextCandidates.copy: Taurus may not argue the moment something feels wrong. They may hold it in, think it through, and respond only when they know exactly what they want to say.
nextCandidates.testedVariable: Conflict-processing style versus a stubbornness label

nextCandidates.title: Taurus Remembers Patterns
nextCandidates.topic: Why Taurus may forgive one disappointment but lose trust when unreliability becomes a pattern
nextCandidates.angle: Focus on Taurus’s attachment to reliability in relationships, especially when someone repeatedly fails to follow through.
nextCandidates.copy: For Taurus, broken promises can change how safe a relationship feels. This explores why one missed commitment may matter less than a pattern of not following through.
nextCandidates.testedVariable: Reliability threshold versus dramatic betrayal framing

nextCandidates.title: When Taurus Needs Help
nextCandidates.topic: Why Taurus may struggle to ask for help even when they are usually the person everyone relies on
nextCandidates.angle: Use a self-worth and attachment angle: Taurus may have trouble accepting help because receiving support can feel like losing control or owing someone.
nextCandidates.copy: Taurus often wants to be the dependable one. This explores why accepting help can feel more uncomfortable than giving it, even when they genuinely need support.
nextCandidates.testedVariable: Difficulty receiving support versus practical-care expression
